units: B. Mets. 8ᵇ יושב לא תפוס במ׳ וכ׳ (not תפיס) he who sits in the wagon has not taken hold of the reins, while he who rides holds the reins (and leads the heterogeneous animals, v. נָהַג).—Esp. (sub. אחז or תפס; cmp. אַפְסָר) taking hold of the reins as a form of taking possession.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 8b:7">Ib.</cite> <he>מ׳ אינה קונה במציאה</he> Rashi a. Ms. R. 2 (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 30) taking hold of the reins does not give possession to the finder.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 8b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>מ׳ מחבירו קנה</he> getting the reins from a fellowman (the owner) means possession.
Ib. מאי לשון מ׳ what is the expression (the etymology of) moserah? (Answ.: from מָסַר).—
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:4">Kidd. I, 4</cite> quot. in Rashi to B. Mets. l. c. <he>נקנית במו׳</he> (ed. <he>במְסִירָה</he>) is taken possession of by seizing the reins (or chain).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 4:9">B. Kam. IV, 9</cite> <he>קשרו … במ׳</he> if the ownertied the animal (to a fence &c.) by the reins.
<cite ref="Mishnah Parah 2:3">Par. II, 3</cite> <he>קיפל עליה את המ׳</he> if he threw the reins over her back.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:4:2">Y. Kidd. I, 60ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>מסר לו מ׳ של וכ׳</he> if he handed him the reins of one of the camels; a. fr.
